cited.title: Computational and neurobiological foundations of leadership decisions
cited.finding: Most participants displayed responsibility aversion (avoiding assuming responsibility for others' outcomes), which could not be explained by guilt, suggesting people associate a psychological cost with responsibility itself
cited.anchor: Interestingly, most participants displayed responsibility aversion, and this effect could not be explained by guilt, suggesting people associate a psychological cost with assuming responsibility for others' outcomes.

cited.title: Choosing for others changes dissociable computational mechanisms underpinning risky decision-making
cited.finding: Being responsible for somebody else's payoffs increases risk aversion
cited.anchor: At least two studies reported that being responsible for somebody else's payoffs increases risk aversion (Fareri et al., 2022; Pahlke et al., 2015)
